messages:
alex: FYI — hit a cluster of preempt evictions in us-west1 during the rolling OS patch, ~6% of streaming sessions dropped. thinking about options to avoid user-visible resets.
kevin: ugh. do we know if most drops are mid-request (streaming) or between requests?
alex: mostly mid-stream (open websocket / long-poll). spikes correlated with spot terminations.
nina: two broad options: 1) proxy that preserves stream state and forwards to a hot-standby; 2) requeue requests with a resume token that clients can replay. both have tradeoffs.
sam: cost-wise hot-standby means reserving some capacity (waste when stable). requeue increases tail latency + client complexity.
kevin: what about a hybrid: cheap ephemeral buffer service (stateless from runtime pov) that holds KV pointers + small replay buffer, not full GPU work. on termination it hands off to next runner which fetches the buffer and continues. keeps GPU free unless needed.
nina: yes — essentially a stream-preserving broker. need secure, short-lived tokens to let a new worker claim a buffer and resume with original KV cache IDs.
alex: prototype token flow in our mind:
```
POST /resume-claim
headers: Authorization: Bearer <signed-requeue-token>
body: { session_id: "s-123", replay_offset: 427 }
```
token signed with KMS, TTL 60s. token includes model-version and kv-prefix to avoid cross-model replays.
kevin: also need idempotency keys so if both the old worker and new one push final events we don't double-apply. simple monotonic offsets should work.
sam: what about networking? if we place the broker in each region (cheap VMs + local object store for small buffers) we avoid cross-region hops during failover. costs tiny compared to reserving GPUs.
infra-bot: [alert] us-west1 spot termination burst 2026-03-15T03:21:14Z (6 instances) :chart_with_downwards_trend:
oncall-bot: opened incident INC-2026-103 for the termination burst, paging oncall rotation.
alex: operational concerns: GC of stale buffers, replay TTLs, and how to surface resume failures to SDK so app can fallback gracefully. SDK should treat resume as best-effort and show partial result if not possible.
nina: edge case: if model variant changed between creation and resume, broker must reject resume or map to compatible quantized variant. include model-hash in token.
kevin: quick implementation plan: 1) minimal buffer broker API + signed resume tokens (2 weeks) 2) runtime adapters to atomically flush small state to broker on preempt signal (1 week) 3) SDK resume logic + UX (1 week)
sam: estimate extra infra cost ~3-5% of current spot spend vs 15-20% if we cold-reserve hot-standby GPUs. seems worth trying.
alex: ok i'll spin up a spike branch for the broker and a runtime signal handler that does atomic snapshot->upload + emit signed token. ping me if you want in. :rocket:
kevin: I'll take the runtime adapter. nina can own SDK changes. sam can model cost delta.
nina: 👍 i'll draft SDK resume API: minimal fields, fallbacks, and error codes.
oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-103 updated: triage completed, monitoring until next patch window.
kevin: one more thought — add metrics: resume_success_rate, avg_resume_latency, buffer_size_hist. we can gate rollout on resume_success_rate > 95%.
alex: agreed. will add to the spike's acceptance criteria.
sam: sounds good. tagging @product later for possible UX notes.
alex: thanks all — keeping this thread as the spike thread.
__notes: messages field is a single continuous string with messages in chronological order
timestamps are unix-like integers as strings
